reasoning: Let a(n) be the number of tilings of a 3×n rectangle by straight 1×3 trominoes. Look at the leftmost column (3 cells). Case 1: it is covered by a single vertical tromino; the rest is a 3×(n−1) board, giving a(n−1) tilings. Case 2: some cell of the column is covered by a horizontal tromino (occupying columns 1–3 in that row). Then the remaining cells of column 1 cannot be covered vertically (a vertical tile needs all 3 rows), so they are also horizontal, and columns 1–3 are exactly filled; the rest is a 3×(n−3) board, giving a(n−3). Hence a(n) = a(n−1) + a(n−3) with a(0)=1, a(1)=1, a(2)=1. Iterating: a(3)=2, a(4)=3, a(5)=4, a(6)=6, a(7)=9, a(8)=13, a(9)=19, a(10)=28, a(11)=41, a(12)=60.
